resources.string: Multiframe needs the camera to capture and merge photo bursts.
Multiframe merges a burst of raw frames to reduce noise and extend dynamic range. No generative AI. Every pixel is measured.
The camera is used for the viewfinder and to capture bursts. Frames are held in memory only until they are merged.
Saved to your device\'s own photo library. The app writes only the files it makes and asks for no permission to read your library.
No network permission. Nothing leaves the phone.
Without the camera there is no viewfinder and nothing to photograph. Allow it to continue.
Camera access was turned off for Multiframe. Turn it on in the system settings to continue.

Every time you press the shutter this app captures a short burst of photographs instead of one, aligns them to cancel out hand movement, and merges them into a single image. Combining frames this way reduces sensor noise, which is most visible in shadows and low light. Tone mapping is kept deliberately restrained rather than heavily processed.

This app does not collect, transmit, or share any personal data. Everything it does happens on your device. There is no analytics, advertising, or tracking of any kind, and no user account. The app does not request internet access. You can choose to share a saved photograph through another app using Android’s share sheet.

Camera access is used only to show the viewfinder and capture photographs. Burst frames are held in memory just long enough to be merged, then discarded. They are never written elsewhere or sent off the device.

Photographs you capture are saved to your device\'s own photo library. The app writes only the files it creates. It does not request permission to read your existing photo library and cannot browse or open pictures taken with other apps. Uninstalling the app does not delete photographs you have already saved.
